title: Trump Sets the First Trilateral Summit With Xi and Putin, the Jensen Huang Espionage Scandal Shakes Nvidia and Washington, and Three Tankers Hit Mines in the Strait of Hormuz
subhead: A tumultuous week across diplomacy, defense, energy, and technology saw the White House and the Kremlin confirm the first-ever trilateral summit between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed a US 'land-for-NATO' proposal; Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid a $450 billion stock rout and congressional subpoenas over a Singapore GPU backdoor to China; and three oil tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz as Turkey enacted the trilateral Mecca Joint Defense Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

sections.heading: Great-Power Diplomacy Shifts to Shenzhen as Washington Proposes Trading Ukrainian Land for NATO Membership
sections.body:
Le Monde, Financial Times, AFP, and Bloomberg — Across the week of November 9–15, Washington accelerated a high-stakes diplomatic campaign to reshape the Eurasian security order ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China. Following preparatory talks in Abu Dhabi and parallel shuttle missions by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Dublin, both the White House and the Kremlin confirmed that US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin will hold their first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen on Thursday, November 19 (Le Monde, Financial Times, The Guardian). By Saturday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly disclosed the core territorial trade-off under discussion: US negotiators had suggested Kyiv cede Russian-occupied territory to Moscow in exchange for Ukraine joining NATO (AFP).

Yet military developments across the European theater showed neither side disarming ahead of Shenzhen. While European capitals categorically rejected Moscow's opening demands that NATO roll back its infrastructure and close bases in eastern member states, Bloomberg reported Saturday that the Pentagon has scaled back previously planned US troop reductions in Europe. Meanwhile, Finland announced it detected a kinetic strike on a Russian warship in the Baltic Sea (Defense News), Romania's Defense Ministry reported Russian drone strikes set fire to a Greek-flagged oil tanker and a bulk carrier near the Danube Delta (Anadolu Agency), Britain and Norway signed a $119.1 million agreement for three mine-hunting drone motherships (Breaking Defense), and Kyiv declared its indigenous FREYJA anti-ballistic missile interceptor operational following the delivery of a Danish radar system (Kyiv Post).
sections.whyItMatters: The Shenzhen summit sets up the first direct three-way negotiation among Washington, Beijing, and Moscow, with Ukraine's territorial integrity and NATO membership directly on the table.

sections.heading: The Iran War Stretches From RAF Mildenhall to Hormuz Mines as Ankara Enacts the Mecca Defense Pact
sections.body:
CBS News, Wall Street Journal, The War Zone, and Anadolu Agency — Eight months into the US-Israeli war with Iran, the conflict expanded in geographic reach even as Washington signaled reluctance to launch new major air campaigns. Early in the week, the US Air Force evacuated its entire fleet of 15 KC-135 Stratotanker aerial refueling aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in England to Germany after intelligence warnings of Iranian-linked retaliation against British bases, and US Air Force security forces subsequently engaged unidentified drones over neighboring RAF Lakenheath for a third time (The War Zone, Le Monde, Times of Israel). Although US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated Friday that Iran's severe economic crisis makes fresh US strikes unnecessary—with Tehran drafting its first zero-oil-revenue budget for 2027 (OilPrice)—US intelligence assessments reported by the Wall Street Journal on Saturday estimated Iran still retains up to 2,500 ballistic and cruise missiles and is actively rebuilding production.

At sea and across the Gulf, physical attrition intensified: Iran's military announced Saturday that three oil tankers caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for removing the Iranian threat 'once and for all' (CBS News), while Saudi air defenses intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles over Riyadh and multiple drones over the Eastern Province (Reuters, Al Jazeera). Against this backdrop, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan formally enacted the trilateral Mecca Joint Defense Agreement uniting Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan—backed by 601 bilateral defense-industry meetings in Istanbul and a new Turkey-Qatar mutual defense agreement—while the Turkish Navy set Egypt as its next joint MİLGEM warship construction partner and placed its İSTİF-class frigate among the six designs shortlisted by the US Navy (Al Jazeera, Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: While Iran uses naval mines, missiles, and asymmetric threats to keep Gulf shipping and Western bases at risk, Turkey is building a formal security bloc stretching from Qatar and Saudi Arabia to Pakistan and Egypt.

sections.heading: Nvidia's $450B Espionage Crisis, Forensic Proof of Blackwell Chips in China, and Dual US Infrastructure Outages
sections.body:
Financial Times, Reuters, TechCrunch, and CNBC — The global artificial intelligence hardware sector suffered its most severe governance shock to date this week after counterintelligence disclosures linked Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang to Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based GPU lessor Megaspeed accused by US officials of funneling restricted American AI chips to Chinese intelligence-linked entities. Following a $450 billion wipeout in Nvidia's market capitalization, Jensen Huang resigned on Friday and was replaced by longtime Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO (Financial Times, Reuters). The House Select Committee on China immediately issued bipartisan subpoenas compelling both Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify under oath—amid reports of a fierce West Wing clash between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Lutnick over lax export enforcement (CNBC, CBS News)—while independent cryptographic researchers produced mathematical proof from floating-point rounding signatures that Chinese labs DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group trained frontier models on smuggled Nvidia Blackwell GPUs (The Register, TechCrunch).

While Elon Musk and 115,000 signatories petitioned Saturday to reinstate Huang, the United States simultaneously weathered back-to-back digital infrastructure failures. Days after a global Microsoft cloud outage disrupted 130,000 users (Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg), the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a four-hour nationwide ground stop across all US commercial flights on Friday that disrupted more than 14,500 flights; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced Saturday that the outage was traced to a contractor upgrade to a legacy L3Harris Technologies telecommunications network and faulty copper wiring, fueling his push for a $50 billion air-traffic control overhaul (CNBC, Ars Technica).
sections.whyItMatters: Jensen Huang's resignation and forensic proof of Blackwell GPUs operating inside Chinese AI labs have shattered confidence in US semiconductor export controls and triggered a major congressional investigation.

sections.heading: Post-Midterm Washington: Hegseth Survives Impeachment, Van Hollen Challenges Schumer, and the US Returns $12B in Venezuelan Oil
sections.body:
AP News, The Guardian, Wall Street Journal, and OilPrice — In Washington's post-midterm lame-duck session, the House of Representatives voted 211–204 to block Republican Representative Thomas Massie's privileged resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over lethal military strikes on suspected Caribbean drug-smuggling vessels (AP News, New York Times). Across the Capitol, after Democrat Scott Colom flipped Mississippi's US Senate seat in the midterms, Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen announced a leadership challenge against Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer ahead of next week's caucus ballot (The Guardian, The Hill).

In global energy markets, the Wall Street Journal revealed Saturday that the US government collected $12 billion from Venezuelan crude oil sales under sanctions-relief mechanisms and returned nearly all of the funds to Caracas, even as Washington released 315,000 barrels of fuel oil reserves to temper winter heating prices (Anadolu Agency) and Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammed Shia al-Sudani fired nine security officials over a $30 million monthly militia oil-smuggling ring (Al Jazeera). Meanwhile, Europe entered the winter heating season with its lowest natural gas storage levels of the 2020s, wholesale European electricity prices spiked past €600/MWh during a wind drought, Germany weighed a €4 billion buyout of nuclear fuel enricher Urenco (OilPrice), and negotiators at the UN COP31 summit in Antalya confronted the loss of the 1.5°C warming benchmark (AFP, CNA).
sections.whyItMatters: Tight energy inventories and Brent crude above $96 are forcing pragmatic policy reversals from Washington's $12 billion Venezuelan oil arrangement to Berlin's €4 billion nuclear fuel investment.

sections.heading: Indo-Pacific Deterrence Hardens in Manila as SpaceX Catches an Orbital Starship Spacecraft for the First Time
sections.body:
Anadolu Agency, South China Morning Post, and Ars Technica — In the Indo-Pacific, Washington and its regional allies moved to lock in maritime deterrence before Thursday's Shenzhen summit. As the 11-member ASEAN summit opened in Manila on Saturday, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed an upgraded bilateral Defense Cooperation Arrangement (Anadolu Agency, The Guardian), building on earlier announcements that the United States and Japan will supply unmanned surface vessels and reconnaissance drones to the Philippine military while Washington demanded Tokyo triple its annual US troop host-nation support payments to $19 billion (USNI News, Defense News). Elsewhere in ASEAN, Indonesia abruptly reversed a planned state monopoly over strategic commodity exports following Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's resignation (South China Morning Post).

The week closed with a historic aerospace breakthrough in South Texas: on Saturday afternoon, SpaceX used the mechanical arms of its Starbase launch tower to catch a returning orbital-class Starship upper-stage spacecraft for the first time after a full day in orbit on Flight 15 (Ars Technica, The Hill, Le Monde), demonstrating the full two-stage reusability needed to support both NASA's lunar ambitions and SpaceX's planned $74 billion orbital and terrestrial AI computing buildout.
sections.whyItMatters: Allied defense pacts in Manila and SpaceX's orbital Starship recovery demonstrate rapid advances in Indo-Pacific maritime deterrence and heavy-lift space capability.

bottomLine: The week of November 9–15 exposed the tension between Washington's desire to broker grand bargains and the realities of contested supply chains and sea lanes: as President Trump prepares to meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen after floating a 'land-for-NATO' formula for Ukraine, naval mines hitting three tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's 2,500-missile stockpile, and forensic proof that Chinese labs trained frontier AI models on smuggled Nvidia Blackwell chips demonstrate that physical corridors and technological export controls remain under relentless pressure.
